points.description: Conclusion from the data: the plastics differ in stretchability, with plastic B stretching the most (about 22-23 mm in both trials) and plastic A (about 10-12 mm) or C (about 13-14 mm) stretching the least. Equivalent conclusions that rank the plastics using the data, such as noting that D is intermediate, also earn the mark.
A valid improvement to the design: use more than two trials (for example three or more) and calculate averages, so that chance variation is reduced.

A valid improvement to the control of variables: keep the sample size (length, width and thickness) the same for every plastic, and use the same mass of weights and the same time for each sample. Other valid controls such as keeping the temperature constant or using a measuring method that gives a more precise reading (for example a ruler or set of marks with a stated resolution) also earn the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks need a data-based conclusion (P1) and two distinct, valid improvements (P2 and P3), each worth one mark. Answers that only restate the table without a comparison, or that give improvements that are not valid for this set-up, earn no mark for that point. Equivalent wording and alternative valid methods earn the marks.
